output.headline: Police hold far-right activist Daniel Thomas on suspicion of endangering life two days after Channel dinghy slashed
output.standfirst: Thirty-seven-year-old arrested on Wednesday night on suspicion of crimes including criminal damage with intent to endanger life, two days after he filmed himself cutting a dinghy while a rescuer was on board
output.bodyHtml:
Police have arrested Daniel Thomas, the far-right agitator and anti-migrant activist, on suspicion of criminal damage with intent to endanger life, two days after he filmed himself slashing the side of a dinghy in the middle of the Channel while a rescuer was on board.

In a statement, Hampshire and Isle of Wight constabulary said a 37-year-old man, of no fixed abode, had been arrested on Wednesday night “on suspicion of destroying ships or fixed platforms or endangering their safety under section 11 of the Aviation and Maritime Security Act 1990”.

Officers also suspect Thomas of “criminal damage, criminal damage with intent to endanger life, and conduct endangering ships, structures or individuals under section 58 of the Merchant Shipping Act 1995”, the police said.

The arrest on Wednesday night appears to have been filmed by Thomas himself. A video uploaded on to his YouTube platform shows the arrest, apparently at a garage, and an officer telling him he had been “involved in criminal damage that has recklessly endangered someone’s life”.

Thomas, who prefers to go by the name Danny Tommo, said: “I understand. I knew this was coming.”

Over the summer Thomas has brought dozens of nationalist protest groups together under the umbrella movement Patriot Platform.

He was also behind this month’s anti-immigration marches by masked men in Dover and Portsmouth.
